AgentDeclarationRequest.description: One declaration: the Control Plane key and the artifact payload.
AgentDeclarationRequest.title: AgentDeclarationRequest

AgentDeclared.description: The registered outcome — the key and its content-hash version.
AgentDeclared.title: AgentDeclared

AgentDefinition.description:
A declared, versioned agent — all six specialization axes (§6.1/§6.2).

SDK-defined (CLAUDE.md §6; D-IMPL-28). The artifact the Agent Factory
interprets and the only supported description of an agent; nothing here is
executable. Changing any axis is a new agent version (channel 1);
capability changes travel through skilling (channel 2) and never touch
this contract.
AgentDefinition.title: AgentDefinition

ApproverIdentity.description:
Who approved: subject id plus identity-provider reference (D-IMPL-21).

SDK-defined. ``identity_provider_ref`` names the provider that
authenticated the subject — the pluggable ``IdentityProvider`` family of
D-IMPL-15 (OIDC/SAML enterprise providers being the realistic
human-principal path, vs. mTLS+JWS for workloads). The SDK enumerates no
provider vocabulary: which providers exist is deployment configuration,
and this contract only requires that the binding *names* one, so replay
can answer "who, per which authority" (D-23 multi-principal).
ApproverIdentity.title: ApproverIdentity

ArtifactPutRequest.description:
One put: the addressing facts and the canonicalizable payload.

**There is no ``tenant_id`` here, and its absence is the contract**
(``SEC-002``). The field used to be the caller's, which made the tenant an
artifact was filed under a thing the caller wrote — so a recognized bearer
could file into any tenant's namespace and the store faithfully obliged.
The tenant is the **capability's** — selected by the gate from the
verified grant's set and read here as ``authorized.tenant``
(:func:`~ccf_runtime.http_api.grants.authorized_from_request`; D-IMPL-353
§1.3) — and comes from nothing else. Deleted rather than kept-and-checked:
a field that must equal a value the door already holds is a field with no
readings left, and every one it could still have is wrong.

Attributes:
    artifact_class: The class the bytes are filed under.
    name: The artifact's name within that class. Together with
        ``artifact_class`` it spells this route's **authorization
        resource**, :data:`ARTIFACT_WRITE_RESOURCE`, so a deployment states
        which classes and names a scope may write rather than granting the
        write verb whole — and the store files under exactly the string
        the authorizer decided on.
    artifact: The canonicalizable payload.
ArtifactPutRequest.title: ArtifactPutRequest

ArtifactRef.description:
A resolvable reference to one stored artifact version.

Attributes:
    content_address: ``sha256`` of the artifact's canonical bytes. This is
        the identity; everything else on this contract is naming.
    uri: The versioned URI, carried as annotation (D-IMPL-26).
    tenant_id: Owning tenant — artifacts are tenant-scoped like everything
        else in the fabric (D-IMPL-05).
    artifact_class: Which class of artifact this is (replay record, policy
        bundle, agent definition, …). Deployment vocabulary; the SDK
        enumerates none of it.
    name: The logical name within the class.
ArtifactRef.title: ArtifactRef

AuthenticationContext.description:
How the approver was authenticated (D-IMPL-21).

SDK-defined. Method, assurance level, and session reference are the
provider's statements carried verbatim — deployment vocabulary the SDK
does not enumerate (mechanism, not values), present so the replay record
can distinguish a strongly-authenticated approval from a weakly-
authenticated one without interpreting either.
AuthenticationContext.title: AuthenticationContext

ConfigRegistered.description: The registered outcome — the key and its content-hash version.
ConfigRegistered.title: ConfigRegistered

ConfigRegistrationRequest.description:
One registration: key, SDK-typed class id, and the artifact document.

Added for the D-IMPL-22 CLI surface (07-11): `ccf skill import` must
register prompt artifacts through the same D-05 versioned path any
client takes, over the wire — the CLI holds no registry handle.
ConfigRegistrationRequest.title: ConfigRegistrationRequest

ConsumedProduct.description:
One Context Product schema an agent reads (axis 2; CLAUDE.md §6.2).

``schema_version`` pins the product class's own lane — a consumer that
names no version consumes whatever the producer ships next, which is a
contract drift replay cannot survive (whitepaper §6.3).
ConsumedProduct.title: ConsumedProduct

ContextContract.description:
Axis 2 — the Context Product schemas an agent reads, and emits to.

CLAUDE.md §6.2. Both directions live here, on one contract, because they
are one axis: what an agent's fabric relationship *is*. The emission side
landed with the assembler surface (``docs/DECISIONS.md`` D-IMPL-97 ruling
2), on the seam this contract's own earlier docstring reserved for it —
*"emission bindings … extend this contract when the ContextAssembly
archetype's transport lands; the shape is additive by design"* — rather
than as a parallel artifact beside it.

**Additive means additive.** ``consumes`` keeps its shape and its
non-empty rule; ``emits`` defaults to the positive
:data:`EMITS_NOTHING` claim, so every shipped definition and every fixture
parses byte-unchanged and means what it meant.

**What is *not* checked here.** That an emitting definition is built from
the ``context_assembly`` archetype, and that the class it emits to is one
the deployment registered, are both refused by
:class:`~ccf.agents.factory.AgentFactory` rather than by this schema. The
schema knows the shape of a document; only the factory holds the archetype
bundles and the deployment's registered classes, and a check that cannot
see both sides cannot name both sides.

Attributes:
    consumes: The product classes this agent reads. At least one — an
        agent that reads nothing has no fabric relationship to declare.
    emits: The product classes this agent assembles and emits, or
        :data:`EMITS_NOTHING`.
ContextContract.title: ContextContract

EmittedProduct.description:
One Context Product schema an agent emits to (axis 2; D-IMPL-97).

The producing counterpart of :class:`ConsumedProduct`, and pinned on the
same reasoning: ``schema_version`` names the class's own lane, because a
producer that named no version would be claiming to satisfy whatever shape
the class takes next — a contract drift replay cannot survive (whitepaper
§6.3, INV-CH7-49).

A separate contract from :class:`ConsumedProduct` rather than a reuse of
it, because the two are read by different mechanism and refused on
different grounds: a consumed class is checked at
:meth:`ccf.agents.agent.Agent.consume`, an emitted class at construction
against what the deployment has registered. Sharing the type would make
"which side is this?" a question the code could not answer.
EmittedProduct.title: EmittedProduct

GrantIssued.description: The issued outcome — the grant's content hash, its D-07 identity.
GrantIssued.title: GrantIssued

GrantRequest.description:
One grant request: the grant artifact plus its pinned definition ref.

No ``actor``: the audited requester is the verified caller (``SEC-002``;
the ``D-IMPL-67`` derivation precedent). ``definition_key`` is this
route's authorization resource, so a deployment states which agent
definitions a scope may skill rather than granting the verb whole.
GrantRequest.title: GrantRequest

GrantRevocationRequest.description:
One revocation: the grant's D-07 identity, and nothing else.

Added for the D-IMPL-22 CLI surface (07-11): §8.3 rules "skill
grant/revoke" for the CLI, the CLI is a thin client with zero
privileged paths, so the revoke verb requires this route — the same
audited :meth:`~ccf.skills.grants.GrantLedger.revoke` transition any
in-process client takes.

No ``actor``: the audited revoker is the verified caller (``SEC-002``).
GrantRevocationRequest.title: GrantRevocationRequest

HitlActionClaims.description:
What the human states and signs about ONE action (D-IMPL-363 E1).

SDK-defined. Every member is something the signer can know from the
served queue view (:class:`~ccf.hitl.transport.PendingHitlEvent`:
``event_key``, ``tenant``, ``product_content_hash``) plus its own
decision, identity, instant and nonce — and nothing the door mints.
``action_time`` is deliberately absent: it is the door's statement,
recorded on the unsigned binding, and the window
:func:`~ccf.hitl.transport.enforce_attestation` applies compares
``issued_at`` against it (E2, E3).

Attributes:
    tenant: The tenant the action is filed under; must equal the
        capability's tenant at verification.
    event_key: The pending event acted on; must equal the capability's
        resource.
    action: The verdict (the :data:`~ccf.hitl.transport.HITL_ACTIONS`
        vocabulary); must equal the presented action and the minted
        binding's ``verdict`` (C1(a)).
    product_content_hash: The content hash of what the human saw; must
        equal the minted binding's.
    subject_id: Who signs; must equal the capability's principal and the
        minted binding's approver.
    issued_at: The signer's own instant — timezone-aware, refused naive.
    nonce: Non-empty and opaque. **Uniqueness per ``(tenant, event_key)``
        is the signer's obligation** (C11(a)); the reference transport
        refuses a reuse atomically. Neither length nor format is relied
        on for that guarantee, and the SDK ships no generator (CINV-01).
HitlActionClaims.title: HitlActionClaims

HitlActionReceipt.description:
The honest submit-only receipt (D-IMPL-62).

SDK-defined. D-IMPL-62 rules the HTTP/CLI HITL action door submit-only:
a submission enqueues on the typed transport and effects no state
transition and no authority action by itself — the owning primitive
resolves it. This receipt is the ruled hardening of that contract:
``status`` is the literal ``"submitted"`` (it cannot state or imply
``resolved`` — the field is type-closed to the one honest word), and
the two disposition fields carry real queue state so the caller sees
the action's disposition rather than inferring it from an echo:
``event_pending`` — whether the submission's event is still on the
tenant's pending queue (it is, immediately after a submit; resolution
is the primitive's act) — and ``submissions_for_event`` — how many
actions the transport has recorded against this event key, this one
included.
HitlActionReceipt.title: HitlActionReceipt

HitlActionRequest.description:
What a caller may say about a human action at a served door (D-IMPL-353 §2 P6).

SDK-defined (CLAUDE.md §8.2/§8.3). The request half of the authority
path — the HTTP ``POST /hitl/actions`` body, and the field set the MCP
``submit_hitl_action`` tool takes as arguments. Deliberately **not** the
submission: the :class:`~ccf.hitl.principal.HumanPrincipalBinding` is
minted by the door from the capability, the verified credential's
:class:`~ccf.hitl.principal.AuthenticationClaims` and the door's clock
(:func:`ccf_runtime.identity_binding.principal_from_authorized`), so this
contract has no ``principal``, no ``subject_id``, no
``identity_provider_ref``, no ``method``, no ``assurance_level``, no
``session_ref``, no ``action_time`` and no ``tenant``. ``extra=forbid``
makes a body that still sends any of them a boundary refusal — and a
caller-typed step-up-MFA claim unrepresentable rather than refused.

What remains is what only the human can state: which event, which
action, the content hash of what they actually saw, an optional
annotation, and — where the HITL policy requires non-repudiation — the
signed :class:`~ccf.hitl.identity_binding.HitlActionClaims` the human
made about this action (D-16; `D-IMPL-363` E1): the ``attestation``, one
object in one shape at both doors (C12(a)), replacing the former signed
copy of the door-minted binding whose ``action_time`` a signer had to
predict.
HitlActionRequest.title: HitlActionRequest

HitlActionSubmission.description:
One human action returning through the authority path (D-IMPL-20/21).

SDK-defined. ``principal`` is required by type: there is no way to
construct a submission without a complete
:class:`~ccf.hitl.principal.HumanPrincipalBinding`, which is how the
no-unrecorded-human-action commitment (CLAUDE.md §8.2) is enforced at
the contract boundary rather than audited after the fact.

**No tenant field (D-IMPL-353 §1.3).** The tenant a submission is filed
under is the capability's — ``authorized.tenant`` at
:meth:`HITLTransportProtocol.submit` — and a second source on the
contract would be a value a door could forget to compare. Deleted, not
deprecated: a document that still carries one is refused at the boundary.
HitlActionSubmission.title: HitlActionSubmission

HumanPrincipalBinding.description:
One human action's complete principal binding (D-IMPL-21; CLAUDE.md §8.2).

SDK-defined. The four D-IMPL-21 fields plus the verdict, all required:
approver identity, authentication context, action time (injected), the
content hash of the Context Product the approver saw, and WHAT THEY
DECIDED. Audit-by-construction holds
regardless of identity provider: no HITL action lands without a binding,
because the HITL action contracts require this type as a field —
omission is a validation error at the boundary, never a null in the
replay record.

At the served doors this is minted by
:func:`ccf_runtime.identity_binding.principal_from_authorized` from the
capability, the verified :class:`AuthenticationClaims` and the door's
clock — the caller supplies the product hash and the verdict, and nothing
about their own identity (D-IMPL-353 §2 P6; SEC-005). The sentence that
stood here until 2026-10-03 said "only the product hash", which this
contract's own `verdict` field made false the moment it was added, and that
description is PUBLISHED in `openapi.json`.
HumanPrincipalBinding.title: HumanPrincipalBinding

InstructionBinding.description:
Axis 6 — one prompt reference plus its declared parameters (D-13).

``prompt`` is a versioned URI; the template text lives in the referenced
:class:`PromptArtifact`, never here (No-Hardcoding Rule, §6.4). This
contract deliberately has no field that could carry inline prompt text.
``parameters`` are the names the binding declares it will supply, validated
against the artifact's own declaration by
:func:`ccf.agents.prompts.validate_instruction_binding`.
InstructionBinding.title: InstructionBinding

LocalCallableBinding.description:
A ``local_callable`` skill's descriptor: a registry key.

A *reference*, never an import. ``callable_ref`` names a key in the
deployment's :class:`~ccf.skills.callables.CallableRegistry`, populated by
explicit registration at the composition root; dispatch resolves it there
and imports nothing, so an entry can only name a callable this deployment
already chose to offer, whatever artifact source the entry arrived from
(D-19; IN-06 — this replaces the I.2 T-05-18 precondition, which MCP and
Peering artifact sources invalidate).

The field's name and ``str`` type are unchanged by that ruling — only the
meaning of the string changed, from a dotted module path to a key — so no
artifact schema version breaks.
LocalCallableBinding.title: LocalCallableBinding

McpBinding.description:
An ``mcp`` skill's descriptor: which server and resource it names.

One of the four types, not the unified mechanism (D-IMPL-12). No MCP
client is constructed from this block in I.2.
McpBinding.title: McpBinding

McpProductBinding.description:
An ``mcp_product`` skill's descriptor: which registered producer to ASK.

`D-IMPL-340`. Dave's definition, verbatim: *"`mcp_product` means: invoke a
registered remote Context Product producer with a governed parameterized
product question."* Its own skill type rather than a second reading of
:class:`McpBinding`, so that a catalog reader can see which entries can
*ask* and which can only *read*, and so the fixed-resource ``mcp`` path is
byte-for-byte what it was.

``server`` selects a **producer registration** by logical name — the
``ccf.mcp-producer`` document the composition root registered — never an
address. ``product_class`` and ``product_version`` are what the producer
is asked for, and the entry's ``produces`` must name the same class: a
skill that says it produces X while asking for Y is refused at
registration, not discovered at admission.
McpProductBinding.title: McpProductBinding

PeeringBinding.description:
A ``peering`` skill's descriptor: the remote peer-endpoint it names.

The token names what class of counterparty the skill reaches — a peer
fabric holding its own Control Plane — never the transport that carries
it (D-IMPL-59 part 1). ``endpoint`` was always a *logical peer-endpoint
name* and never a URI, so the field was about a peer from the start.

A descriptor, not a transport: Peering admission verification (CLAUDE.md
§7.2) applies when products actually cross the boundary, which no code
in this wave does.
PeeringBinding.title: PeeringBinding

PendingHitlEvent.description:
One pending HITL event awaiting a human (D-IMPL-20; CLAUDE.md §8.2).

SDK-defined. The typed record the ruling specifies: event class,
workflow state reference, the identity of the Context Product the human
must see (its D-IMPL-26 content hash — the same identity the
:class:`~ccf.hitl.principal.HumanPrincipalBinding` echoes back, so
"what was shown" and "what was approved" are comparable byte for byte),
and the deadline/escalation policy reference, pinned.
PendingHitlEvent.title: PendingHitlEvent

PerspectiveBinding.description:
Axis 3 — the Π role-conditioning shaping the agent's view (§6.2).

``selection_params`` is deployment vocabulary; the SDK enumerates none of
it. Values are strings because they participate in canonical serialization
and therefore in content identity — a float here would make the agent's
identity platform-dependent.
PerspectiveBinding.title: PerspectiveBinding

ProcedureBinding.description:
A ``procedure`` skill's descriptor: a pinned instruction reference.

SDK-defined (D-IMPL-56; CLAUDE.md §6.2 channel 2, §7.3 seam 1). The
instruction content travels by reference — an
:class:`~ccf.agents.definitions.InstructionBinding` naming a versioned
prompt artifact — and is consumed on seam 1 (context injection) **only**.
A procedure never becomes a seam-2 tool: smuggling instruction text into
the tool surface would hand the harness authored prose the Control Plane
never versioned (T-07-05), so the binding deliberately has no field that
could carry inline text (No-Hardcoding Rule, CLAUDE.md §6.4).
ProcedureBinding.title: ProcedureBinding

SignedHitlAction.description:
The claims together with their detached JWS (D-IMPL-21; D-IMPL-363 E1).

SDK-defined (CLAUDE.md §8.2); D-IMPL-66(a). The claims travel in the
clear — audit consumers read them without keys — and the signature is the
detached compact JWS (``protected..signature``) exactly as
:mod:`ccf.peering.identity` produced it over the claims' canonical
bytes. A verifier recomputes those bytes from :attr:`claims`, so a
signed copy and a delivered copy cannot silently differ. This is the
``attestation`` a :class:`~ccf.hitl.transport.HitlActionRequest` and a
:class:`~ccf.hitl.transport.HitlActionSubmission` carry, at both doors
in one shape (C12(a)).

Attributes:
    claims: The signed claim set.
    signature: The detached compact JWS, ``{protected}..{signature}``.
    key_id: The key identifier the signature was made under — the
        claim the verifier holds against the protected header's ``kid``
        and against the pinned policy's per-subject key map (E5).
SignedHitlAction.title: SignedHitlAction

SkillArgumentElement.description:
An array's element spec: a primitive, or an object of members.

The *"lists-of-objects (sufficient for the UBO owner list)"* half of
D-IMPL-103. An array is transparent to the depth count — a list of
objects is one level of nesting, not two, because the array is a
container of the object rather than a level of its own — which is why
this type may declare members while :class:`SkillArgumentMember` may not.

It deliberately has **no** ``items`` field, so a list of lists is not
expressible: that would be a second container level the ruling does not
admit.

Attributes:
    type: The declared JSON Schema type of one element.
    description: What one element is.
    properties: For an ``object``-typed element, its members. ``None`` —
        the default — is the positive statement *this element declares no
        members*, which for a non-object type is the only coherent
        statement and is why the field agrees with ``type``.
    required: Which of those members must be present. A subset.
SkillArgumentElement.title: SkillArgumentElement

SkillArgumentMember.description:
A member of a nested object — the deepest a declaration may go.

D-IMPL-103's ceiling, expressed **structurally**: this type has no
``properties`` and no ``items`` field, so a third level is not something
a declaration can be refused for — it is something a declaration cannot
say. That is a stronger reading of *"one level of nesting ... depth 2 is
the ceiling, not a floor"* than a validator, which is a rule someone can
later relax; a missing field is not.

Attributes:
    type: The declared JSON Schema type.
    description: What the member is for. Required with no default, the
        same D-16 forcing function that applies at every other level.
SkillArgumentMember.title: SkillArgumentMember

SkillArgumentProperty.description:
One argument's typed spec on a catalog entry (D-IMPL-56, D-IMPL-103).

JSON-Schema-shaped by construction: ``type`` is a closed Literal over the
JSON Schema primitive type names, and ``description`` is required with no
default — the same D-16 forcing function as the entry description,
because a property whose meaning an adapter would have to invent is the
same defect one schema level down.

**The D-IMPL-103 widening, and what it did not change.** Dave ruled
(2026-08-11) that this declaration supports *one* level of nested objects
and lists-of-objects — enough for a beneficial-owner list, whose pairing
a flattening into parallel arrays degrades to an index convention the
schema cannot state. The ruling is explicit that it is a **widening, not
a replacement**: ``properties``, ``items`` and ``required`` all default to
"not declared", so every declaration written before the widening is still
valid, still means what it meant, and still renders byte-identically —
an unset nesting field is not a declaration and contributes nothing to
:meth:`SkillArgumentSchema.to_input_schema`'s output.

**One level is a ceiling, and the ceiling is structural rather than
checked.** The nested types are :class:`SkillArgumentMember` (which has no
nesting fields at all) and :class:`SkillArgumentElement` (which has
members but no ``items``), so depth 3 and a list of lists are not
declarations this contract can express. The alternative — one
self-referential type plus a depth validator — was written first and
rejected: it expresses the ceiling as a rule a later author can relax,
and it additionally made FastAPI split every model reaching it into
``-Input`` / ``-Output`` variants in the published OpenAPI document,
renaming ``SkillCatalogEntry`` in a contract external integrators read.

Attributes:
    type: The declared JSON Schema type.
    description: What the argument is for. Required, never adapter-authored.
    properties: For an ``object``-typed property, its own typed members.
        ``None`` — the default — is the positive statement *this property
        declares no members*, which for a non-object type is the only
        coherent statement and is why the field agrees with ``type``.
    items: For an ``array``-typed property, the spec every element must
        satisfy. ``None`` by the same discipline.
    required: For an ``object``-typed property, which of its own members
        must be present. Empty by default, and a subset of ``properties``.
SkillArgumentProperty.title: SkillArgumentProperty

SkillArgumentSchema.description:
The typed argument declaration on a catalog entry (D-IMPL-56).

JSON-Schema-shaped and MCP-``inputSchema``-compatible, pre-specified:
``properties`` maps argument names to typed specs, ``required`` is a
subset of the property names, and the rendered surface always pins
``additionalProperties`` to ``false`` at **every** object level —
structurally, mirroring this contract's own ``extra=forbid`` closed
world. One shared derivation (:mod:`ccf.skills.toolsurface`) renders it
into every harness.

**This is also the declared payload schema of a Context Product class**
(D-IMPL-97 ruling 1, D-IMPL-103 branch (i)). ``ccf.products.payload``
names it ``ProductPayloadSchema`` and *aliases* this type rather than
copying it: the ruling measured a nesting-capable sibling at five
duplicated symbols and declined it, because D-IMPL-97 asked for reuse of
the machinery already proven rather than a second one.
SkillArgumentSchema.title: SkillArgumentSchema

SkillCatalogEntry.description:
One versioned skill catalog entry (D-IMPL-12; CLAUDE.md §6.2 channel 2).

SDK-defined. The artifact the grant machinery (05-06) binds against by
version — a grant references an entry, never copies it, so upgrading a
skill is a new entry version and a new grant, both audited.

Two-field versioning per D-IMPL-28: ``schema_version`` is this class's
lane; ``artifact_version`` is the author's content claim, hash-verified
at registration (D-05).

``description`` and ``argument_schema`` are required with no default and
no sentinel (D-IMPL-56; D-16): the tool surface every harness renders is
a declared artifact property, produced by the one shared derivation in
:mod:`ccf.skills.toolsurface` — never adapter-authored prose.

``produces`` (D-IMPL-336) declares the Context Product **class** this skill
emits, by ``schema_name``. It is the mirror of
:attr:`SkillRequirements.required_context_products`, which declares what a
skill *reads*: placing both on one artifact makes a skill's context
footprint readable in one place — what it consumes, what it emits, what
policy it needs.

Four properties of ``produces``, each a decision:

* **One class per skill.** A skill needing to emit two classes is two
  skills, which is what keeps requirement resolution a lookup rather than
  a search.
* **A class name, never a version, a payload shape, or an instance.** The
  child's ``schema_version`` is *observed* at composition and checked
  against the requirement's declared range
  (:class:`~ccf.products.contract.ChildRequirement`); it is not predicted
  here, and version compatibility stays the product's own semver lane
  (INV-CH7-49).
* **:data:`NO_PRODUCT_CLASS` is a positive statement** — *this skill emits
  no governed product* — and not silence (D-IMPL-38). A skill at the
  sentinel **cannot satisfy a composite requirement**.
* **Hash-transparent at the sentinel** (D-IMPL-243), so every catalog entry
  registered before this field existed keeps its artifact identity and
  every grant against one stays valid.

``produces`` lives on the entry rather than on the grant because a grant
binds an entry *by reference and by version* and copies nothing: two grants
of one entry must not be able to disagree about what that skill emits.
SkillCatalogEntry.title: SkillCatalogEntry

SkillGrant.description:
One skill grant — a declared, versioned Control Plane artifact.

CLAUDE.md §6.2 channel 2; D-IMPL-12/29. A grant *references*, never
copies: the agent by definition content hash (D-IMPL-26 canonical
identity) and the catalog entry by pinned version — upgrading a skill is
a new entry version and a new grant, both audited. The grant's own
content hash is its identity and the member the D-07 grant-set hash is
computed over.

Two-field versioning per D-IMPL-28: ``schema_version`` is this class's
lane; ``artifact_version`` is the author's content claim, hash-verified
at registration (D-05).
SkillGrant.title: SkillGrant

SkillRequirements.description:
The typed requirements declaration on a catalog entry (D-IMPL-29).

The block the tier-1 policy-compatibility check (05-06) compares against
an agent's policy regime and context contract — structurally, as
subset/equality over opaque identifiers. Both members are required with
no default: an empty frozenset is the author's explicit statement that
the skill needs nothing of that kind, which is not the same statement as
silence (D-IMPL-38).

Attributes:
    required_scopes: Policy-regime identifiers this skill's dispatch will
        require. Opaque to the SDK; declared by the deployment.
    required_context_products: Context Product classes this skill reads.
        Opaque to the SDK; held against the agent's context contract.
SkillRequirements.title: SkillRequirements

ToolBinding.description:
A ``tool`` skill's descriptor: the command/entry it names.

Descriptor fields only — the SDK stores what the deployment declared and
ships no execution surface for it here (D-08; dispatch is 05-06 scope).
ToolBinding.title: ToolBinding

TraceEntry.description:
One recorded state transition in an execution's trace (CLAUDE.md §8.1).

SDK-defined. Frozen and canonically serializable, so the trace the
engine serializes for replay dimension 5 is byte-stable: the same
execution serializes to the same block, and the block is recorded
verbatim (07-05).

Attributes:
    sequence: Position in this execution's trace, from zero. Ordering is
        the entry's own claim, never inferred from timestamps.
    source: The state the machine left.
    target: The state — or, for an exception routed to a handler, the
        pinned handler ref (D-13) — the machine moved to.
    kind: Which category of event this was (:data:`TRACE_ENTRY_KINDS`).
    occurred_at: Timestamp from the engine's injected clock.
TraceEntry.title: TraceEntry

VersionedRef.description:
A pinned ``ccf-artifact://`` reference (axes 4 and 5; D-IMPL-26).

A ref, never the artifact: the policy bundle and the debt profile are
Control Plane artifacts with their own lanes, and inlining either into a
definition would give one document two version identities.
VersionedRef.title: VersionedRef

WorkflowCompleted.description:
A terminal outcome, with the replay handoff the engine serialized.

``step_sequence_block`` is the canonical serialization of the execution
trace — serialized once, here, and passed verbatim to replay dimension 5
(07-05 keyword); ``delegation_chain`` extends dimension 4 with the
workflow execution id followed by the agent-definition identities the
execution invoked, in declaration order (CLAUDE.md §8.1).
WorkflowCompleted.title: WorkflowCompleted

WorkflowExceptionRouted.description:
An exception path taken to its ref'd handler — an expected outcome.

First-class recorded transition (D-13; CLAUDE.md §8.1): the node's
exception ref resolved and the execution's state was handed to it. A
node with *no* ref never produces this — absence propagates to the
reserved ``failed`` terminal instead (D-IMPL-61 option-a).
WorkflowExceptionRouted.title: WorkflowExceptionRouted

WorkflowInvocationRequest.description: One invocation: the pinned definition reference and an execution id.
WorkflowInvocationRequest.title: WorkflowInvocationRequest

WorkflowResumptionRequest.description: One resumption: the same pinned reference plus the human's decision.
WorkflowResumptionRequest.title: WorkflowResumptionRequest

WorkflowStateRecord.description:
One execution's live state on the Control Plane seam (D-IMPL-18/27).

SDK-defined. The typed, opaque record the engine writes through the
audited surface and validates on read (isinstance, foreign-record typed
error) — the ``GrantStateRecord`` discipline applied to workflows. Keyed
``(tenant, execution_id)`` so two tenants running the same workflow
definition concurrently never collide (D-23).

Attributes:
    tenant: Owning tenant of this execution.
    execution_id: Caller-supplied execution identity within the tenant.
    current_state: The node the machine is at.
    status: Where the machine is in its lifecycle
        (:data:`WORKFLOW_STATUSES`).
    trace: Every transition recorded so far, in order.
    workflow_definition_uri: The pinned versioned URI of the workflow
        definition this execution runs (D-IMPL-26).
    started_by: The principal that started the execution (SEC-006;
        `D-IMPL-366` G1 (a)); ``None`` on a pre-change record.
    workflow_definition_hash: The content hash of that definition —
        what actually binds the execution to it. The URI alone does
        not: it is built from the artifact's OWN declared tenant, name
        and artifact_version, so a second definition registered under a
        different Control Plane key carries an identical URI while
        declaring different routing. Resume compares this, so an
        execution never continues under a definition it was not started
        with — the thing the URI check already claimed and could not
        deliver (SEC-001, security review 2026-09-23).
WorkflowStateRecord.title: WorkflowStateRecord

WorkflowSuspended.description:
A typed suspended handle — suspension is a value, not an exception.

Returned when execution reaches a hitl-gate node (CLAUDE.md §8.1). The
gate interaction in 07-06 goes through the injected HITL transport stub
only; the real ApprovalGate (07-07) owns gate semantics.
WorkflowSuspended.title: WorkflowSuspended

info.description: Typed HTTP front door over the fabric's existing extra=forbid contracts, mirroring the D-IMPL-22/23 ruled noun set (CLAUDE.md §8.3; EXPR-03). Every request to this API is authenticated and authorized before it is routed: there is no unauthenticated arm, no path is exempt, every route declares the action identifier its authorization is decided under, and what each action reaches is the deployment's own versioned scope mapping rather than any default this API ships.
info.title: CCF HTTP API
